idea-plugin.name: Ruby Analysis Probe + Patch
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin modifies RubyMine's behaviour at runtime. It works around a defect in anonymous symbol identity that can stop Ruby code analysis from ever completing.

The defect. AnonymousDefiningCallType.getAnonymousClassName derives an anonymous class/module's fully-qualified name from (textRange.hashCode() << 15) ^ text.hashCode() alone. The containing file is not part of the identity, so N files whose anonymous defining call has identical text at an identical offset — e.g. several monkeypatch files each starting with ActiveRecord::Base.class_eval do — collapse into one symbol. That merged symbol resolves to zero index elements, and ancestor resolution for it does not converge.

RubyMine tries to stop this twice and both guards miss. SymbolHierarchy.getAncestorsCaching keys RecursionManager.doPreventingRecursion on Pair(symbol, invocationPoint), so re-entering for the same FQN through a freshly built Symbol instance is not seen as recursion; and getAncestorsFromAnonymousDefiningCalls checks a visited set that is allocated per getAncestorsCaching call, which is the very boundary the cycle crosses.

The patches, both toggleable from the tool window and both restricted to synthesized $$ANON FQNs so ordinary resolution is untouched:

  • Cut anon cycles — a per-thread guard keyed on the FQN string. Re-entering getAncestorsCaching for an anonymous FQN already being resolved on the same thread returns an empty list, which is what the method itself returns when its own recursion guard trips. Because the cut lands before RecursionManager is consulted, the outer frame's mayCacheNow() is no longer forced false, so results can actually be memoized.
  • Suppress empty lookups — anonymous stub keys measured to return nothing are served empty for up to 2s at a time instead of re-querying the index. Roughly half of all CPU during a stall was inside RubyStringStubIndexExtension.getElements returning nothing.

Known trade-off: a cycle-cut ancestor list may be incomplete and is now cacheable, so an anonymous class's hierarchy can be missing entries. Uncheck Cut anon cycles to restore stock behaviour.

Also reports what analysis is doing: the symbol being resolved, its source location, recursion depth, stub-key histograms, and how many cycles have been cut. Opens under View > Tool Windows > Ruby Probe. While analysis is wedged for more than 10s a snapshot is appended to ~/ruby-probe-stall.log from a background thread, so the data survives an unresponsive UI.
